questions.prompt: A fact table is declared at order-line grain. Someone loads one row per order with the total quantity. What breaks first?
options: Product-level questions: an order with three products can only point at one product_key
questions.explanation: At order grain a row can't carry one product per line, so revenue by product or category is wrong. Mixing grains is the most common dimensional modeling error.

questions.prompt: Customer 3 moves from the US to Germany on 2025-07-01. With SCD Type 1, what happens to revenue by country for her February orders?
options: It moves to DE, so last quarter's report silently changes
It's split between US and DE
questions.explanation: Type 1 overwrites the attribute in place, so every historical fact now joins to DE. Type 2 keeps the old row (and key) for old facts.

questions.prompt: Why can't dim_customer use customer_id as its primary key under SCD Type 2?
options: Natural keys are slower to join
One customer_id has several versions (rows), so it isn't unique
questions.explanation: Each change adds a row for the same natural key. A surrogate key identifies one version, and facts reference that exact version.

questions.prompt: An SCD2 load re-runs the same snapshot twice on the same day. What should the second run do?
options: Add another version for every customer
Nothing: every incoming row equals its current version
questions.explanation: Comparing against the is_current row makes the load idempotent. After the first run the current rows already hold the new values.
